title: Bhooth Bangla Just Hit Netflix. Akshay Kumar and Priyadarshan Finally Got Their Reunion Right.
excerpt: The horror-comedy that earned ₹264 crore worldwide is now streaming globally. If you missed it in theatres, your excuse just expired.
body:
There's a particular kind of magic that happens when Akshay Kumar walks onto a Priyadarshan set. It happened with Hera Pheri. It happened with Garam Masala. It happened with Bhool Bhulaiyaa. And after years of audiences wondering whether lightning could strike again, Bhooth Bangla proved that yes — when these two decide to be funny, the box office clears the way.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XW1RkKiRnsg

The horror-comedy, which hit theatres on April 17 and ran for over six weeks, has just landed on Netflix as of June 12. For diaspora audiences in the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf who couldn't catch it during its theatrical run — or those who did and want to relive the mayhem — the wait is over. Netflix has it globally, in Hindi, and ready to stream.

And what a run it had. Bhooth Bangla earned approximately ₹198 crore net in India and crossed ₹264 crore worldwide, a certified hit against its ₹120 crore budget. The numbers are impressive, but even more impressive is the fact that the producers had already recovered nearly all of their investment before the first ticket was sold. Netflix reportedly paid ₹60 crore for the digital streaming rights alone. Zee Cinema secured satellite rights for ₹25 crore. Zee Music Company took the music rights for another ₹10 crore. That's ₹105 crore in non-theatrical revenue before the opening credits rolled in a single cinema.

"I was not trying to reinvent the wheel. I was trying to make people laugh until it hurt." — Priyadarshan

The film reunites Akshay with a cast that reads like a greatest-hits lineup of Indian comedy. Tabu brings her signature intensity to a role that keeps you guessing. Wamiqa Gabbi, who's been quietly building one of the most interesting careers in Indian cinema, holds her own against Akshay's physical comedy with a performance that's both sharp and grounded. Paresh Rawal does what Paresh Rawal does — steals scenes with the precision of a surgeon. Rajpal Yadav delivers the kind of unhinged energy that only he can sustain for a full runtime. And somewhere in the chaos, Asrani shows up to remind you that legends don't retire, they just pick their moments.

The premise is classic Priyadarshan: a sprawling, allegedly haunted mansion, a motley crew of characters who have no business being there, and a series of escalating misunderstandings that spiral into full-blown pandemonium. It's broad, it's loud, and it's unapologetically committed to being a paisa vasool experience.

What makes this particular reunion meaningful is context. Akshay Kumar spent the better part of the last few years searching for a hit. After a string of underperformers that would have buried a lesser star, Bhooth Bangla arrived like a declaration: the audience never stopped loving the comedy Akshay. They stopped loving the films that forgot to let him be funny.

Priyadarshan understood the assignment. He didn't try to make Akshay carry a social message or anchor a patriotic thriller. He put him in a haunted house, surrounded him with brilliant comedic actors, cranked up the absurdity, and let the man work. The result feels loose, lived-in, and — crucially — like everyone on screen is actually having a good time.

For the Indian diaspora, the Netflix release is the real event. Theatrical windows in international markets are unpredictable — some cities get day-and-date releases, others wait weeks. Netflix erases that friction entirely. You can watch Bhooth Bangla tonight on your couch in New Jersey, Brampton, Birmingham, or Dubai, no FOMO required.

The ₹264 crore global total also reinforces something the industry has been slow to accept: horror-comedies are bulletproof. The genre has produced hit after hit — Stree, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2, Munjya — while expensive action spectacles regularly underperform. Audiences want to laugh and scream in equal measure, and the formula shows no signs of fatigue.

Bhooth Bangla is now streaming on Netflix in India and worldwide.
